implement: legion-worker: the implementer's own part of it — the pull-request body and its proof rules (references/pr-body.md), the push and handoff rules, the default-branch identity check before a push, and review-thread resolution as the pull request's author; this change is a daemon change delivered as one image a person pins, so the proof rules decide what the phase may complete on.

ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass legion-worker's pr-body reference requires over the settled head before completion, which matters here because the change touches manifest.go's environment builders, podsafety and plugins.go at once.

dispatch: every write to the issue (a question for the architect is an Envoy message, but a standalone human to-do — the deployment repository's own pod.env check — is a dispatch ask, and the plan names one).
test: legion-worker: the tester's part — it drives the changed surface rather than rerunning CI, reads CI for lint, types and the unit suites, and records its own proof; the plan's acceptance table names the exact Go test invocations and the in-pod exercise it must be able to re-run.
dispatch: the tester writes its verdict and anything the human must know through the dispatch command, never a GitHub issue.
review: legion-worker: the reviewer's part and its merge-gate and review-thread references — the order of a review round, what counts as evidence, and that retro and READY follow its approval of a head.
dispatch: the reviewer's communication with the architect and the issue goes through the dispatch command.

findings.finding: F1: the plan's claim that no daemon-to-image contract bump is needed contradicts version.go's own bump rule, which names manifest.go's mainEnvironment as part of the contract; entry 18 bumped for exactly this kind of value-only change (the per-role state home).
findings.answer: Accepted: the plan now bumps DaemonAPIVersion 32 to 33 in the same commit (task 4), with the numbered entry, packages/contracts/fixtures/daemon-api/version.json regenerated by the Go golden test's -update, packages/pi-legion/package.json's legion.daemonApiVersion moved with it, and the renumber-collision check against every published pi-legion version run before the number is taken.

findings.finding: F2: 'the install is made to copy rather than hardlink' has two readings. Legion runs a bun install of its own (plugins.go installScript's `bun add` into pluginsRoot under the role's XDG_STATE_HOME, which this change moves onto the volume beside the role's bun cache); that one is both achievable and provable by the pod builder's Go tests, while an agent's own project install is not Legion's to flag.
findings.answer: Adopted: task 3 adds --backend=copyfile to installScript's `bun add`, which is the reading the spec's own proof method (the Go tests of the pod builder) can check, and plugins_test.go asserts it. The other reading is recorded as the plan's one spec departure and sent to the architect.

findings.finding: F3: the spec restates TestBunCacheHomeIsMountedFromNoVolume's reason as cross-filesystem copying, but the test's own words give another reason — the cache is private to one pod and dies with it. After the change a hardlink-corrupted cache survives every pod replacement for the issue's life.
findings.answer: Named in the plan's departure section with its bound (a cache per role; one Legion-made checkout per volume, workspace.Location) and its recovery (delete /legion/scratch/<role>/bun and install again), and sent to the architect as the decision it owns.

findings.finding: F4: the plan's subPath-mount scheme contradicted its own test (TestUvKeepsItsPythonsAndCacheOnTheIssueVolume requires SubPath == ""), added 42 mounts per pod, and solved a problem that mostly does not exist: go and bun create their own cache directories and the shim already makes the state home. Only TMPDIR has no creator.
findings.answer: The mounts are dropped. Task 2 has the shim make every told scratch directory (podsafety.EnsureScratch beside EnsureStateHome), so the paths stay on the issue volume's own mount and the new test asserts the same shape the uv test does.

findings.finding: F5: if a kubelet-made nested subPath directory came up root-owned and not group-writable, every role's shim would refuse to start, and the fix would need another image build and human apply.
findings.answer: Removed with the mounts (F4): the shim creates the directories as the pod's own user, which the volume's mode already allows, so no unproven kubelet behaviour is on the path.

findings.finding: F6: XDG_STATE_HOME carries Oh My Pi's logs, Chromium's browser profiles and the installed plugin generation onto the issue volume, where today they die with the pod; docs/kubernetes.md promises the opposite.
findings.answer: In the plan's documentation task (the lines that say a pod which dies loses those files) and in the architect's list, with the sizing. Unbounded growth is not a new risk for the plugin generations: installScript removes every earlier generation before it installs.

findings.finding: F7: the spec's ~1.2 GB measured need carries no bun figure, yet bun's install cache is the largest item (1.4 GB for this repository) and the per-role split multiplies it.
findings.answer: The plan carries the measurement and the arithmetic (about 14 GB if all six roles build, against a 20 GiB volume nothing prunes) in the architect's list, with the existing remedy named (issue_volume is an operator setting, whose default the spec's non-goal keeps). The plan changes nothing about sizing.

findings.finding: F8: after this change a full volume also stops a pod from starting, because the shim cannot make its state home; today a full volume leaves the roles running, and nothing watches free space.
findings.answer: Recorded in the architect's list as a changed failure mode.

findings.finding: F9: adding four names to runtimeOwned refuses, at boot, any deployment whose runtime.kubernetes.pod.env sets one of them.
findings.answer: In the architect's list as the one thing a person with the deployment repository must confirm before the digest is pinned, and in the implement phase's dispatch ask.

findings.finding: F10: the operator's mount fence for the agents' state home guards a path no role uses once the state home moves.
findings.answer: Task 1 keeps the row with its reason rewritten (it is the setup container's state home now; the roles' scratch is under TreeRoot, already fenced) and updates the three operatorpod_test.go rows and the documentation paragraph.

findings.finding: F11: nine further surfaces — the eight golden manifests, controller_test.go's exact variable list, live_operator_test.go's pod-baseline check, scripts/e2e/README.md's state-home row, api/version.go's entry 18 text, pi-legion's manifest and changelog, config/kubernetes.go's reservation comment, and four docs/kubernetes.md passages.
findings.answer: All folded into tasks 4, 5 and 6 by name.

findings.finding: F12: four acceptance lines have no decidable check as written (the restart record, the deployment's reservations block, what counts as 'nothing under the home directory', and how a path is read off the mount table).
findings.answer: The plan's acceptance table and production-check section give each one a command: read_record at the start and end of the check window for the restart record; jj diff over defaultResources plus a grep of deploy/kubernetes/ plus a human's confirmation for the reservations block; a named list of paths that must be absent with the image's two shipped artefacts excluded by path; and findmnt -T <path> -o SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE per path.

findings.finding: F13: moving TMPDIR is in the spec's list but supported by none of its measurements, and the issue's disk is slower.
findings.answer: Kept, with its reason stated: a role container mounts no /tmp, so its temporary files are charged to the same gigabyte (docs/kubernetes.md, Anatomy of a Sandbox pod), and the spec accepted the disk's cost. Named to the architect as a point it may overrule.

findings.finding: F14: 'the browser directory Playwright downloads into' is listed among what the runtime points at by name, but is absent from the acceptance's seven directories.
findings.answer: Settled by measurement rather than a new variable: Playwright follows XDG_CACHE_HOME on Linux, which the plan records with the command that shows it, so the told list stays seven and the production check covers the browser. Named to the architect.

findings.finding: F15: 'uv's download cache stays shared between the roles of a tree' describes something narrower than it sounds, since each issue has had its own volume since LEGION-632.
findings.answer: The plan restates the check as TestUvKeepsItsPythonsAndCacheOnTheIssueVolume passing unmodified, and requires the scratch root not to overlap uv's directories.

findings.finding: F16: the spec's claims about Autopilot's clamp and its 10 GiB per-pod ceiling, and the 1 GiB per container that follows, were checked and hold (scripts/e2e/README.md's Stage 4a rows, docs/kubernetes.md's Autopilot section, config/kubernetes.go's 1Gi requests).
findings.answer: Nothing to answer; the plan builds on them.

findings.finding: F17: the departure's argument rests on the volume holding one checkout, which needs its citation.
findings.answer: The departure cites workspace.Location (podkind.go's prepare) and says the argument covers the Legion-made checkout alone.

findings.finding: F18: the proof step proved the manifest and the environment, not the two things that could fail in the cluster (the kubelet's directory creation and 42 mounts per pod).
findings.answer: Both failure modes are gone with the mounts (F4). The proof is now the rendered pod plus a real run of the rendered environment in the implementer's own pod, with the production check deciding the cluster's half; the plan also warns the implementer not to run bun's install as a negative control on the container filesystem, since that is what killed the planner's own container.

specDepartures.spec: The replacement rule for the bun cache is two rules together: each role gets its own directory, and 'the install is made to copy rather than hardlink, the way uv is already made to copy for exactly this reason'; the acceptance line reads 'bun installs by copying files out of its cache rather than hardlinking them into the workspace, now that the two share one filesystem.'
specDepartures.plan: Each role gets its own bun install cache on the issue's disk, and the one install Legion itself renders (the plugin install in plugins.go's installScript, which lands under the role's state home beside that cache) carries --backend=copyfile. An agent's own `bun install` into the workspace is left hardlinking out of that role's cache, because nothing Legion sets can change it.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured in this issue's pod on 2026-10-20 with bun 1.3.14: `bun install --backend=copyfile` gives one link per file, while the same setting in a project bunfig.toml or in the global $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bunfig.toml is silently ignored (the installed file and the cache file are one inode) and an invalid value is not rejected; no environment variable exists. Upstream agrees: oven-sh/bun#25391 and oven-sh/bun#32158 are open requests for the setting. Keeping the cache off the volume instead is not available: a cold `bun install --frozen-lockfile` of this repository fills a 1.4 GB cache, larger than the gigabyte a role container is admitted with, and measuring it on the container filesystem killed this planner's own container. The damage is bounded by a cache per role and one Legion-made checkout per volume (workspace.Location, podkind.go).

acceptance: bun installs by copying files out of its cache rather than hardlinking them into the workspace, now that the two share one filesystem. — narrowed to the install Legion renders itself; an agent's own project install hardlinks from its role's cache, and a file edited in place under node_modules changes that cache entry until the issue closes.
